root_cause.text: The register tracking bitmap marks user-controlled `len` bytes as initialized during `nft_exthdr_init()`, but when `NFT_EXTHDR_F_PRESENT` is set, the eval path writes at most 4 bytes (1 byte for success, 4 bytes on TCP/DCCP error), causing registers beyond the written region to retain uninitialized stack data.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the check `if ((flags & NFT_EXTHDR_F_PRESENT) && len != 1) return -EINVAL;` to reject `len` values other than 1 when the PRESENT flag is set, because the eval path only writes a single byte (`nft_reg_store8`) for existence checks. The commit message states: "When len > 4, registers beyond the first are never written, retaining uninitialized stack data from nft_regs."
